text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT SALE - Armenia bought 62,927 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat under the PL 480 program for shipment January 23 to February 6, USDA said. The wheat was purchased from Farmland Industries at a cost of $180.48 per tonne FOB, USDA said.

BARLEY SALE - The Cyprus Grain Commission on Friday bought two 25,000-tonne cargos of barley from Toepfer Athens, the company said. It accepted the first bid at $145.36 per tonne and the second at $144.36 per tonne C and F. Shipment dates were not available.
WHEAT TENDERS - Lebanon's economy ministry plans to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard wheat later this month, the government said.

- Bangladesh seeks 100,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 wheat or Australian standard or better Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21. Offers are to be opened January 18 and results announced two to three days later.
CORN TENDER - News was awaited on South Africa's Maize Board tender for 15,000 tonnes of yellow maize for either export or domestic use. The offer was expected to close January 16.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDERS - Taiwan Sugar Corp. will tender for a combined 30,000-tonne U.S. corn and soybean cargo on Tuesday, traders said. The shipment will consist of 20,000 tonnes of corn and 10,000 tonnes of soybeans. Shipment dates will be for February 25 to March 10 delivery from the U.S. Gulf or March 10 to March 25 from the Pacific Northwest.

- Taiwan's Hui Shung Group passed on a tender for a combined shipment of 38,500 tonnes of U.S. soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 corn because of high prices, traders said. No retender schedule was set.
RICE TENDER - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs is seeking to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for March shipment. Results would be February 13.

MARKET TALK - Australia's 1.5 million tonne wheat sale to Iran was priced at about the same level as the recent sale, or about $185 per tonne, to Pakistan, an Australian Wheat Board official told Reuters.
- Syria has offered 50,000 tonnes of hard amber durum wheat for sale, the country's general establishment for cereal processing and trade said. The final date to receive bids is January 21.
- The Canadian Wheat Board signed a pact to sell one million tonnes of wheat to Thai flour mills over the next five years. The business was worth C$250 million at current wheat prices.
- Yugoslavia, facing an acute grain shortage after its worst harvest in 25 years and excessive exports in 1995/96, is in the process of importing 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes of wheat, producers said.
